playbook:
When I can afford a settlement immediately, I build the settlement rather than a road.

When I can afford only a road and not a settlement, I build the road to secure at least one point.

When I cannot build anything this round, I will consider posting one targeted trade offer to the player most likely to have the resource I need, offering a single resource for a single resource.

I will not post an offer if no other player currently holds the resource I need; posting a useless offer wastes the one allowed slot.

When proposing a trade, I prefer 1-for-1 exchanges, matching noncritical surplus resources I have to the resource I lack.

When choosing which player to target, I prioritize players who have recently given away the resource type I need or who currently hold that resource, rather than players who are hoarding it.

I will not post offers that would leave me unable to build in the upcoming build phase unless the trade clearly enables a better immediate build (e.g., converts surplus into the exact missing resource for a settlement).

When an offer is posted to me that would give me a resource I need for an immediate build and asks for a resource I have in surplus, I accept.

When an offer is posted to me that would give me a resource I already have spare but asks for the only copy of a scarce resource I need for an immediate build, I refuse.

I refuse trades that would trade away my only copy of a single resource required for an immediate build (for example, my only wood when I can build a road or settlement that uses it).

I will not accept trades that do not change my ability to make a higher-value build this round or that convert a valuable long-term resource (like ore) into a lesser immediate gain unless I have clear surplus and the trade enables a higher-score build.

I avoid multi-resource offers unless I am desperate and the multi-resource trade clearly secures an immediate settlement or otherwise changes the game's outcome for me.

I do not make multi-party or vague offers; every offer names the counterparty and exact resource quantities.

If a player repeatedly trades away a resource type for a different resource type, I prioritize offering that player reciprocally when I need that resource.

If repeated small offers fail to secure the one resource I need and trading further would cost me resources needed for a higher-value build, I conserve my resources instead of escalating trades.

If no player can supply the missing resource (e.g., everyone lacks wood), I do not waste an offer and instead prepare resources for future rounds.

When I hold resources valuable for later (e.g., ore for a city/dev card) I will decline trades that give me resources I do not need now at the cost of losing the ability to build a higher-value item this round.

I check my holdings and projected build in the upcoming build phase before posting or accepting any trade; decisions prioritize ensuring I can complete the highest-value immediate build available.

1.text:
When I can afford a settlement right now, I build the settlement rather than a road.

When I can afford neither piece, I build none.

When I need one specific resource to complete a settlement this round, I post a single offer giving one resource I have a surplus of and requesting that specific resource, and target a player who visibly has surplus of it or who recently traded away other resources (they may want what I give).

I will not post offers that give away a single-copy resource I need for a future settlement (e.g., my last brick, grain, ore, or wood) unless doing so still leaves me able to build the settlement this round and is clearly beneficial.

I accept posted offers only if accepting them leaves me with the exact resource mix required to build a settlement this round (prefer a single offer that enables a settlement over multiple offers that would not).

If multiple posted offers would enable a settlement, I accept exactly one — the one that costs me the least strategically scarce resource.

If accepting any posted offer would require giving up a scarce resource that prevents me from building this turn or the next, I accept none.

When choosing a counterparty to target with an offer, prefer players who visibly hold the resource or who have recently shown willingness to trade (recent trades away from them suggest they might accept what I offer).

Do not try to squeeze an extra road if a settlement is immediately affordable — take the higher-point play right away.

Do not refuse every trade reflexively to hoard flexibility; accept a single trade that converts otherwise unusable holdings into the exact set needed for a settlement.

If I cannot complete a settlement this round and no acceptable trade is available, avoid giving away resources that improve opponents’ ability to build immediately (don’t make trades that clearly enable an opponent’s settlement unless I get equivalent enabling value).

When posting offers late in the game (final round), prioritize trades that could immediately convert into a settlement this same round; otherwise post none.

2.text:
I build a settlement immediately whenever I already have one of each resource at the start of the build phase.

If I can currently build only a road but can plausibly reach a settlement next turn (through likely trades or minor yields), prefer to aim for the settlement rather than taking the road.

Never post an offer that spends resources I need to build in the current build phase.

When I have a single-resource surplus and need exactly one of some other resource to build next turn, post a 1-for-1 offer trading that surplus for the needed resource to a specific player who currently has that resource.

When posting an offer, always name a real counterparty who has shown the resource recently; avoid anonymous or open offers.

Prioritize trading away common excesses (wood, grain, ore) to obtain a missing common building resource (especially brick) rather than hoarding the excess.

If an offered trade would give an opponent the exact final resource to build immediately while only marginally helping me, refuse unless I gain at least equivalent immediate benefit.

Accept posted offers that give me a needed resource and only ask for something I can spare, provided acceptance does not enable an opponent to build immediately at my expense.

When multiple posted offers together would let me build next round, accept all net-beneficial offers that still leave me able to build (do not accept offers that leave me short in the build phase).

Avoid making any trade that would leave my recorded holdings negative at the end of the trading phase; do not accept trades that create or worsen negative balances.

When I need a specific scarce resource (e.g., ore to fix a negative), prioritize offering grain or another spare resource to a player who holds that scarce resource rather than offering resources that would enable them to build.

Do not rely on accumulating only wood (or any single resource) — secure brick (and other distinct build components) early through targeted trades so I can convert holdings into points.

Keep offers simple and 1-for-1 where possible; complex multi-resource trades are less likely to be accepted and harder to coordinate in short rounds.
